newsitem.title: UK: Signs of EMU chaos alarms Euro markets.
newsitem.headline: Signs of EMU chaos alarms Euro markets.

text.p: French and German shares were badly shaken on Monday by renewed market fears over European economic and monetary union (EMU), while the franc and dollar also weakened.
The worries were triggered when France's new Socialist-led government called for a "period of reflection" on a pact limiting budget deficits of countries that join a single European currency.
"This all begs the question - how is the euro going to be achieved?," said one Frankfurt share dealer.
"One thing is sure, if people really start to worry about this, there will be chaos in the markets," he added.

Analysts said the French demand, which amounted to a delay in the timetable for ratification of the so-called stability pact, added more uncertainty to the creation of the euro, but did not spell the end of EMU.
The Paris Bourse, which was trading lower before the comments, slid to 2.2 percent down but then rebounded off its lows and ended with a loss of just 1.2 percent, down 33.05 points at 2,686.20.

The franc fell by more than half a centime to 3.3825 per mark, but held above last week's low of 3.3860 set after the combined left swept to power in a June 1 election upset. In late business it was at around 3.3798.

French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn called on Monday for a period of reflection before agreeing to the stability pact. But he said France was not seeking to renegotiate the pact and was totally committed to a timely EMU start in 1999.

Europe's key stock markets opened strongly following Wall Street's record close on Friday when it rose 130 points, but only London managed to stay in the plus column throughout the day, though it too suffered profit taking during the morning.

London shares drew comfort from Wall Street's continued bull run -- the Dow Jones index was up almost 60 points at the European close -- and the FTSE ended 41.7 points, or almost one percent higher, at 4,686.7.
German shares turned sharply lower after a strong start, as the upsurge in worries about monetary union offset initial optimism about U.S. economic prospects.
Sheer vertigo was another factor behind the downturn, traders said, as the thinly-traded market simply failed to sustain the record highs achieved in early trade.

The blue chip DAX index closed the floor session down 27.86 points, or 0.8 percent, at 3,667.43 points -- dropping nearly 70 points from the historic intraday high of 3,734.05 points set in pre-bourse electronic dealings.

The dollar slid sharply on the EMU worries, always a negative for German exporters, and confidence was further hurt by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel's dogged insistance on strict fulfilment of Maastricht budget goals -- a scenario widely viewed as impossible for cash-strapped Germany.

In currencies, the dollar ended more than 1-1/2 pfennigs and more than two yen lower in Europe, weighed down by a combination of concerns about European monetary union and U.S. protests at swelling Japanese trade surpluses, traders said.

The mark was lifted after the French reservations about the details of the post-EMU budgetary stability pact were expressed at the European Union finance ministers meeting in Luxembourg, adding to jitters about a delay to the 1999 EMU start date.
The yen led the way in early trading, however, pushing the dollar down to a six-month-low about 111.80 and extending the Japanese unit's gains since May 1 to 12.3 percent.
At 1530 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7063 marks compared with 1.7261 late in Europe on Friday. Against the yen, the dollar was at 112.55 compared with 115.23 late last week.
"Dollar/yen was the mover overnight but it's all been dollar/mark and EMU-related trading since then," said Adrian Schmidt, international economist at Chase Investment Bank.

"The mood surrounding EMU is nervous but there is still an underlying confidence it will go ahead on time," said Schmidt. "What we have realized, however, is that the mark is still being played as the European safe-haven - on the knee-jerk at least."
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 1.7063 marks and 112.55 yen compared with 1.7261 marks and 115.23 yen in late European trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 41.7 at 4,686.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 33.05 points at 2,686.20.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 27.86 points at 3,667.43. The Ibis DAX of post-bourse electronic trading stood at 3,668.61.

PRECIOUS METALS CLOSING PRICES Gold closed virtually unchanged at $344.25, from $344.45 on Friday, after trading in narrow range all day. Silver was off four cents at $4.83. Platinum ended at $466.50 down from $490.00. Palladium was little changed at $226.00, up some $2.00.
